     POST HEARING BRIEF OF INTERVENOR CBF RANCH LLC (PARTY 196)

     Intervenor CBF Ranch LLC (Party 196) files its post-hearing brief.

     1.      CBF Ranch LLC is an entity owned by James Bradley Curlee and Betsy Figer

     Lambeth, who are married and own property on Segment E11. Their testimony was

     timely filed under Item No. 4181 on the Interchange and admitted into evidence at

     the ALJ Hearing on June 8, 2026.

     2.       CBF Ranch LLC objects to any transmission line route that includes segment

     link E11. The evidence presented demonstrates that no certificate of convenience

     and necessity should be granted for any route that includes Link E11 for at least the

     following reasons.

          a. Of all the proposed routes, those which include E11 directly impact the most

             habitable structures – contrary to accepted standards and policies.

          b. Link E11 would pass within 500 feet of Intervenor’s habitable structure. This

             structure was completed in December 2025 but not identified on the Applicant’s

             latest Intervenor map.

          c. Link E11 would prevent the Intervenor’s intended use of its property as a

             residence of peaceful respite, family gatherings and pecan orchard.
             d. The routes that would include link E11 would run along and nearly parallel to

               Salado Creek on Intervenor’s property, approximately 1,500 feet – contrary to

               accepted standards and policies.

            e. The routes that would include link E11 would require clear-cutting woodlands

               located in riparian and riparian-upland areas along Salado Creek on

               Intervenor’s property. That clear-cutting would destroy seven large oaks, four

               of which are estimated to be over 200 years old; a pecan grove containing

               160 pecan trees; and numerous other native trees and shrubs that are

               important to flood control and wildlife, contrary to accepted standards and

               policies.

The need for the proposed certi cate of convenience and necessity is doubtful. If the ALJs

and/or the Public Utility Commission nd that such a need exists, the route should not include

Link E11.

                                                             Respectfully submitted,
